text: Let us begin with the document itself. This is Department of Expenditure Office Memorandum number 2 slash 4 slash 2022 E two B, dated the thirtieth of December, twenty twenty two. It supersedes every earlier instruction on House Rent Allowance. The compendium applies to all civilian employees of the Central Government. It also applies to civilian employees paid from the Defence Services Estimates. There is one group students often forget: these orders also apply to persons serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. Now the trap. Two groups are outside these rules: employees appointed on ad hoc or personal rates of pay, unless their appointment order specifically allows House Rent Allowance; and staff paid out of contingencies, that is casual employees and labour. Remember: the compendium covers all civilian Central Government staff, Defence civilians, and Audit and Accounts Department staff, but excludes ad hoc and contingency paid employees.

text: Paragraph 1.1 is short but decisive. Pay, for calculating House Rent Allowance, means the pay drawn in the prescribed Level in the Pay Matrix under the Seventh Central Pay Commission. And note the exclusion: no other type of pay is counted. Special pay, and similar additions, stay out of the House Rent Allowance calculation. Now family. Paragraph 1.2 says family means the Government servant's wife or husband, children, and other persons residing with and wholly dependent upon him or her. Here is the trap examiners love. A husband, wife, child or parent with an independent source of income is not treated as family, unless that income, including pension and its benefits, does not exceed nine thousand rupees per month. Remember: pay for House Rent Allowance is the Pay Matrix level alone, and the family income cut off is nine thousand rupees per month.

text: Paragraph 1.3 gives three limbs. Same station means all places contiguous to the qualified city under Paragraph 3.2, plus places dependent on it under Paragraph 3.4, plus places inside the Urban Agglomeration of that city. Paragraph 1.4 takes the definition from the latest Census Report of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India. An Urban Agglomeration is a continuous urban spread made of a town and its adjoining outgrowths, or contiguous towns. Why does this matter? Because during leave, deputation abroad, training or suspension, your House Rent Allowance depends on retaining a house at the same station. These two definitions decide what counts. Be careful with this trap. An Urban Agglomeration is determined by the Census Report, not by municipal boundaries and not by local usage. Two different tests, two different consequences. Remember: same station covers contiguous, dependent and Urban Agglomeration areas, and the Urban Agglomeration comes from the Census Report.

text: Paragraph 2.1 is clear. Classification of cities for House Rent Allowance is based on the population of the area, as per the latest Census Report. The first class is X. Any city or town with a population of fifty lakh and above falls in X class. Y class covers populations from five lakh up to fifty lakh. Z class covers everything below five lakh. Any place not listed as X or Y is treated as Z. Now the trap. This compendium only fixes the population criteria. The actual list of cities in each class is notified by separate Department of Expenditure orders, the latest being the Census twenty eleven reclassification of December twenty nineteen. Remember: X is fifty lakh and above, Y is five to fifty lakh, Z is below five lakh, and the test always comes from the latest Census.

text: Excellent question, and this is the single most important correction in the whole course. The table printed in the Office Memorandum gives the base Seventh Pay Commission rates: twenty four per cent for X, sixteen for Y, and eight for Z. But read the note below that table. When Dearness Allowance crosses twenty five per cent, the rates automatically rise to twenty seven, eighteen and nine per cent. And when Dearness Allowance crosses fifty per cent, they rise again, to thirty, twenty and ten per cent. Both of those triggers have already fired. Here is the trap. The revision is automatic. The Department of Expenditure confirmed in August twenty twenty one that no separate House Rent Allowance order is issued when Dearness Allowance crosses these levels. So you will never find an order saying thirty per cent. Remember: twenty four, sixteen and eight is only the base rate. Both Dearness Allowance triggers have already fired, so today's rate is thirty, twenty and ten per cent.

text: Here is the current position. Dearness Allowance crossed fifty per cent with effect from first January, twenty twenty four. That crossed the second and final threshold, so House Rent Allowance moved to thirty, twenty and ten per cent of basic pay. Dearness Allowance today is sixty per cent of basic pay, with effect from first January, twenty twenty six. That is Office Memorandum 1 slash 1 sub one slash 2026 E two B, dated twenty second April, twenty twenty six. And there is a floor. House Rent Allowance is never less than five thousand four hundred rupees in X class, three thousand six hundred in Y, and one thousand eight hundred in Z. Those figures are thirty, twenty and ten per cent of the minimum pay of eighteen thousand. And here is the trap. Dearness Allowance at sixty per cent does not give you a further House Rent Allowance step. The ladder has only two rungs, at twenty five and fifty per cent, and both are behind us. Remember: House Rent Allowance is thirty, twenty and ten per cent since January twenty twenty four, Dearness Allowance is sixty per cent since January twenty twenty six, and there is no third rung on the ladder.

text: Short answer: no, not official. The Eighth Central Pay Commission was formally constituted by Gazette resolution dated third November, twenty twenty five. It is chaired by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on tenth August, twenty twenty six, the Ministry of Finance confirmed the Commission has not submitted its recommendations yet. It has eighteen months from constitution, so the report is due around May, twenty twenty seven. It is still in the consultation phase. text: The answer is the place of duty. Paragraph 3.1 says House Rent Allowance is admissible with reference to the place of duty of the Government servant, irrespective of whether he is residing at that place or anywhere else. Paragraph 3.2 fixes the boundary. The locality is the named municipality or corporation, and it also includes suburban municipalities, notified areas or cantonments that are contiguous to it, plus any other area the Central Government notifies. Paragraph 3.3 removes any doubt about change. If a State Government includes an area within, or excludes it from, the municipality or Urban Agglomeration, these instructions automatically apply or cease to apply from that very date. So the trap is this: living elsewhere does not by itself defeat your claim. What matters is the place of duty. But remember, the separate conditions in Paragraph 5 can still bar you on other grounds. Remember: House Rent Allowance follows the place of duty, not where you sleep, and boundary changes apply automatically from the date the State Government makes them.

text: Yes, possibly. Paragraph 3.4 says staff working in Central Government establishments within eight kilometres of the periphery of the municipal limits of a qualified city get that city's House Rent Allowance rates, even if they do not reside within those limits. But there are conditions. First, a certificate in the Annexure One format must be obtained from the Collector or Deputy Commissioner having jurisdiction, and the Administrative Ministry must refer it to the Department of Expenditure for initial sanction for a period of three years. Extensions beyond the initial three years may be allowed by the Administrative Ministry in consultation with its Financial Adviser, and by the Comptroller and Auditor General for staff serving under him. The certificate of dependency is obtained from the Collector. Here is the precise trap. The eight kilometre rule continues only at places within eight kilometres of the municipal limits which are NOT included in the Urban Agglomeration of any city. If the place is inside a Urban Agglomeration, the Urban Agglomeration rule applies instead. Remember: eight kilometres, a Collector's certificate and a three year sanction, but only where the place is not already inside a Urban Agglomeration.

text: Paragraph 4.1 is the starting point. The allowance is not admissible to those who occupy General Pool Residential accommodation provided by the Government. Paragraph 4.2 covers departmental pools. Where Government quarters are available for the staff of specified Departments or for specified categories of staff, the prescribed procedure for applying for allotment has to be followed. Paragraph 4.3 answers your question precisely. House Rent Allowance stops from the date the accommodation is actually handed over in an immediately habitable condition. And on surrender, it becomes payable again from the date of surrender. Two traps here. First, an officer debarred from allotment for unauthorised sub letting still gets House Rent Allowance during the debarment. Second, a Government run or subsidised hostel bars the allowance, but if the hostel charges market rent on commercial lines, it does not. Remember: a Government quarter ends the allowance, it stops on handing over in habitable condition, and a subsidised hostel also bars it, while a commercial rent hostel does not.

text: Paragraph 4.6 gives you a window. If you retain Government accommodation at the old station on normal rent, penal rent, or even unauthorisedly on market rent, you may draw House Rent Allowance at the new station for up to eight months from the date of transfer. Paragraph 4.7 covers a different case. If you had no Government accommodation at the old station and leave your family behind because you have not rented a house or been allotted one at the new station, you stay eligible at the new station until you are allotted accommodation there. Paragraph 4.8 is the hard stop. In either case, House Rent Allowance under these provisions is not admissible beyond the date on which Government accommodation is allotted to you at the new station. And the ninety day trap. For a transfer of ninety days or less, you draw the old rate. Beyond ninety days, the rate follows the new place of posting. If a short transfer is later extended, the switch happens from the date of the extension order, not from the date of transfer. Remember: eight months if you retain the old quarter, it stops on allotment at the new station, and ninety days is the point at which the rate switches.

text: Paragraph 5.1 sets three absolute bars. You cannot draw House Rent Allowance if you share Government accommodation allotted to another Government servant, or live in accommodation allotted to your parent, son or daughter by Government or a public body, or if your spouse has been allotted accommodation at the same station, whether you live there or separately. Now your case. Paragraph 5.2 says you remain eligible if you share private accommodation with another Government servant, provided you pay rent or contribute towards rent, house tax or property tax. The amount does not matter. But there is a limit. Where two employees share accommodation allotted to another Government servant, House Rent Allowance is admissible to only one of them, at their choice. And here is the contrast examiners test. If husband and wife are both Government servants living in hired or owned accommodation, both draw House Rent Allowance as per their own entitlement. That is completely different from the Paragraph 5.1 bar, where the spouse has been allotted Government accommodation at the same station. Remember: paying rent makes sharing acceptable, an allotted spouse quarter is fatal to the claim, but both spouses in a hired or owned house both get paid.

text: Yes, but not as House Rent Allowance. Paragraph 5.5 allows reimbursement of the rent actually paid when you stay temporarily in a State Bhavan, Guest House or Departmental Guest House run by the Central Government, a State Government or an Autonomous Organisation. There are five conditions. You must not have been allotted Government accommodation, the guest house must be at your place of posting, you must produce rent receipts, the reimbursement runs for a maximum of six months, and no House Rent Allowance is paid during this period. So the outer limit is six months. Beyond that, the concession simply does not run. The trap is the either-or. During this period you get the reimbursement instead of House Rent Allowance, never both together. One is based on the percentage of pay, the other on the rent actually paid with receipts. Remember: guest house rent is reimbursed for up to six months, and no House Rent Allowance is paid during that period.

text: Paragraph 6.1.1 gives the general rule. You draw House Rent Allowance during leave at the same rate as before, for leave not exceeding one hundred and eighty days, and for the first one hundred and eighty days of any longer spell. Terminal leave is excluded. Paragraph 6.1.5 adds the paperwork. Beyond the first one hundred and eighty days, on grounds other than the medical grounds in 6.1.6, you must furnish the certificate prescribed in Annexure Three. Paragraph 6.1.6 is the humane exception. For employees suffering from tuberculosis, cancer or similar ailments on medical certificates in the prescribed form, the limit extends from one hundred and eighty days to eight months. Two final traps. If you take leave and then resign without joining duty, the authority must recover the entire House Rent Allowance drawn before accepting the resignation. But if leave on medical grounds beyond one hundred and eighty days ends in retirement on invalidity, no recovery is made. Remember: one hundred and eighty days is the general limit, eight months for tuberculosis and cancer, Annexure Three beyond that, and full recovery if you resign instead of rejoining.

text: Paragraph 6.2 covers joining time: you continue at the rate of the station from which you were transferred. Paragraph 6.3 covers deputation abroad: you stay eligible for as long as your family remains at your last place of duty in India, subject to the Annexure Three certificate. For training abroad, Paragraph 6.4 gives you the rate of the station you were deputed from, and leave during the training earns nothing. For training in India, Paragraph 6.5 is generous: you may take whichever is more favourable, the place of training or your place of duty. Paragraph 6.6 covers suspension: the allowance continues, but beyond one hundred and eighty days you need the Annexure Three certificate. Paragraph 6.9 is simple: during tour, your entitlement is regulated with reference to your headquarters. And the two traps. For re-employed pensioners, Paragraph 6.7 computes House Rent Allowance on pay plus pension, subject to the ceiling of the maximum pay of the post. And for employees outside the Fundamental Rules and the C.C.S. Leave Rules, Paragraph 6.8 allows only forty days, extended to one hundred and eighty for tuberculosis, cancer and similar ailments. Remember: training in India gives you the better of two rates, tour follows your headquarters, and staff outside the Fundamental Rules get only forty days.

text: Paragraph 7.2.1 is the main one. Every Government servant must furnish a certificate in the Annexure Two form along with the first claim for House Rent Allowance. Paragraph 7.2.2 splits the audience. Non-gazetted officers furnish the certificate to their Head of Office; gazetted officers furnish it to their Accounts Officer. Paragraph 7.2.3 puts the duty on the Drawing and Disbursing Officer, who must endorse two certificates on the bill: that eligibility has been verified against the Ministry of Finance order, and that the prescribed certificates have been obtained and the claims are in order. And the most valuable trap of this chapter. You no longer need to apply for Government accommodation or furnish a No Accommodation Certificate. That condition was dispensed with by the Department of Expenditure order of third May, twenty nineteen. Annexure Three is still required for the specific cases listed in Paragraph 7.3. Remember: Annexure Two goes with your first claim, the Drawing and Disbursing Officer endorses the bill, and the No Accommodation Certificate has been abolished.

Card three. House Rent Allowance follows the place of duty. The eight kilometre rule is residual and needs a Collector's certificate. Government accommodation bars the allowance, but sharing is fine if you pay rent or contribute to tax.

Card four. One hundred and eighty days of leave generally, eight months for tuberculosis and cancer, forty days for staff outside the Fundamental Rules. Annexure Two with the first claim, Annexure Three for the listed cases, and the Appendix records the earlier orders now superseded.
Remember: place of duty governs, thirty, twenty and ten per cent applies today, one hundred and eighty days on leave, and Annexure Two goes with your first claim.

text: That brings us to the end of this masterclass. Keep three things in mind. First, House Rent Allowance follows your place of duty, not where you live. Second, the printed twenty four, sixteen and eight per cent is only the base rate; today you draw thirty, twenty and ten per cent. And third, the Eighth Pay Commission figures you see online are demands, not law. Keep revising, and see you in the next chapter.
